correctness.rationale: Odd exactly three-deficient-perfect integers are squares by parity. Rational upper bounds exclude p>=7, p=5 with r>=13, and p=3 with q>=37. All remaining p=3 q choices are exhaustively reduced to 23400 3-signature quadratic equations, each having at most one positive root. Exact integer discriminants, division, primality and direct proper-divisor checks return exactly four witnesses on three integers. The isolated p=5,q=7,r=11 case is exhaustively excluded. The embedded Python standard-library checker was executed on the new source and reproduced all expected integer counts. No finite prime cutoff is used to justify infinity.

value.rationale: The odd three-deficient-divisor parity lemma forces even prime exponents; p^2q^2r^2 is therefore the mathematically canonical first multiplicity layer for exactly three distinct prime factors. A complete unbounded classification of this natural layer, including all exceptional divisor triples and their non-uniqueness at 27225, advances the two-prime literature and supplies a sharp baseline for larger exponent layers. This is not a routine bounded enumeration.
